key_insight: GRPO can directly steer a crystal generator’s discrete atom-type transitions toward desired materials rewards, substantially improving targeted structure yield while revealing reward-hacking risks.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical reinforcement-learning route for inverse materials design, enabling black-box optimization of crystal generators for properties beyond imitation of training data.
method: Apply group-relative policy optimization to a stochastic-interpolant / discrete flow-matching crystal generator.
Update policy on discrete atom-type transition likelihoods rather than only latent or continuous denoising variables.
Use explicit safeguards to limit reward exploitation and track performance by reference-hull context.
evidence_signal: The reinforced model raised metastable, unique, and novel (mSUN) yield from 13.4% to 45.5% on a community benchmark, with additional analysis split by the number of reference phases.
watch_item: Directly optimizing discrete atom-type transitions can exploit the reward function, so guards and benchmark reporting must prevent inflated scores from trivial single-element packings.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning on the Discrete Composition Channel of a Crystal Generator: Validated Gains and Reward Hacking
